questions.stem_text: Sociology differs from common sense in that:

options.A: it focuses on the researchers' own experiences
options.B: it makes little distinction between the way the world is and the way it ought to be
options.C: its knowledge is accumulated from many different research contexts

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - its knowledge is accumulated from many different research contexts

questions.stem_text: Which of the following is not a 'research purpose'?

options.A: a religious organization that claims total spiritual authority over its members
options.B: a church organized around voluntary rather than compulsory membership
options.C: a sect or cult with a very small following
options.D: a hierarchy of priests or other spiritual leaders

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - a religious organization that claims total spiritual authority over its members

questions.stem_text: In Durkheim's work, the term 'collective representations' refers to:

options.A: effervescent ceremonies that create a feeling of belonging
options.B: images of gods or totems that are widely recognized
options.C: shared ideas and moral values, often symbolized by an object or figurehead
options.D: ideological tools used to obscure class divisions

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - shared ideas and moral values, often symbolized by an object or figurehead

questions.stem_text: The terms 'crisis of the 1970 s' is used to refer to:

options.B: the eradication of the welfare state
options.C: rising divorce rates and the decline of the traditional family
options.D: an unfortunate twist in fashion sensibility

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - declining profits and rising unemployment
